architectureDecisions: Use Next.js Metadata API and metadata route conventions rather than manual head tags.
Keep crawl-critical identity in server-rendered modules while preserving the client animation component.
Use one validated public-origin helper for canonical, social, sitemap, robots, and JSON-LD URLs.
Do not invent backend, database, API, or authentication layers for a frontend-only SEO scope.
Use a dependency-free regression script instead of adding a test dependency for static SEO markers.
Keep semantic landing-page content in Server Components and isolate canvas/GSAP/ScrollTrigger in a focused Client Component.
Use a bounded four-worker frame queue with an 18-frame critical window and four-settled-frame readiness threshold.
Use an additive 768x512 WebP brand asset for static imagery while preserving the legacy PNG until compatibility is audited.
Treat the homepage as B2B/store-first based on repeated store-facing copy, pricing, and dashboard evidence while preserving current consumer-facing wording pending owner confirmation.
Create only four distinct factual routes: store use case, workflow, pricing, and FAQ; do not publish thin keyword variants or unapproved legal/consumer pages.
Use one shared metadata helper, visible breadcrumbs with matching BreadcrumbList JSON-LD, and a route registry as the sitemap source of truth.
Do not add FAQPage JSON-LD because current Google search appearance guidance does not make regular FAQ rich results a reasonable expectation for this commercial site.
Use a server-rendered Blog presentation with an explicit external public-content provider boundary; do not add a local CMS, database, editor, or authentication layer.
Render only validated published Blog records, keep empty/no-CMS content noindex and out of the sitemap, and sanitize Markdown with raw HTML disabled.
Use request-time sitemap generation so CMS outages preserve static marketing URLs and newly published indexable articles can be discovered without a rebuild.
Use one safe JSON-LD serializer for repository-controlled and validated article/breadcrumb data; remove the unverified Blog subdomain from Organization sameAs.
Use a deterministic 1200x630 Open Graph image route with minimal supported text after validating the installed image renderer.
Keep CMS and public site as separate applications; expose only validated published content and use server-only HMAC revalidation.
Version the immutable 535-frame sequence under public/frames/v1, preserve its content signature, and apply long-lived caching only to the versioned path.
Expose Google Search Console HTML-tag verification only from a validated server/build environment variable; omit verification metadata when configuration is absent or invalid.
assumptions: https://rookhposh.ir is the canonical public origin.
Persian is the only published language in this repository.
The existing logo asset remains the Organization logo; the social-card surface uses the deterministic /opengraph-image route until dedicated approved artwork is supplied.
The initial browser asset inventory is a tool observation, not a protocol-level request trace.
The connected browser surface cannot force reduced-motion emulation or provide Lighthouse/field data.
The connected browser surface cannot force mobile viewport emulation; those checks remain environment-limited.
risks: Social platforms may crop the existing 1536x1024 logo asset.
External dashboard, blog, and trust-seal availability is not controlled by this repository.
Live Search Console/rich-result verification is not available locally.
The existing 535-frame visual experience remains a large client asset workload by design.
The R2 JavaScript chunk reduction is intentionally small because static-content decoupling is primarily a rendering and scheduling improvement.
No field Core Web Vitals or Lighthouse score is available from this environment.
Homepage intent remains owner-confirmation pending; the implementation does not silently rewrite the current H1 or positioning.
Approved legal copy and routes remain unavailable, so Terms and Privacy pages are intentionally unpublished.
The final public route set is intentionally small; additional routes require distinct factual content and owner-approved intent.
Blog authoring and content availability remain external through optional BLOG_CONTENT_API_URL; the first-party public routes belong to this application.
RSS exposes published indexable articles only; noindex content remains public-page controlled but is excluded from sitemap/feed discovery.
Public CMS fetches accept remote HTTPS origins only; loopback HTTP is allowed for local integration smoke tests.
The versioned frame path must be included in every deployment artifact; future frame-content changes require a new versioned path.
Search Console ownership, indexing, ranking, query, page, CTR, and field Core Web Vitals data require owner-controlled external access and are not available in this repository.
